answer: To stop a farm from minting votes, run a bonded uniqueness lottery. Each epoch an agent commits a hidden nonce bound to its public key, then reveals it against the network seed. Tickets that collide, reuse entropy, or arrive late forfeit the posted stake. A factory can still mint names, but every extra ticket needs its own bond and fresh randomness. When collisions cluster, the slash sends a ripple through the whole lotus of related keys and drains that lagoon of cheap identities before any of them unlocks voting weight.
